newsitem.title: USA: Dole may pour resources into Calif. - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Dole may pour resources into Calif. - newspaper.

text.p: Aides say Republican presidential nominee Bob Dole has tentatively decided to pour resources into California, a newspaper reported Monday.
The New York Times said Dole campaign strategists met over the weekend to decide where to allocate funds and energy in the crucial weeks ahead of the election.
The Times reported there was near-unanimous agreement that an all-out effort should be made in vote-rich California.

President Clinton has courted California throughout his first term, making more than two dozen visits to the state. Clinton has led Dole in voter-opinion polls in California throughout the campaign, but a Field Poll last week showed the Republican challenger had cut the president's lead in that state to 10 percentage points from 20-plus in earlier surveys.
Aides said Dole had not signed off on the California plan, but he indicated during a meeting Saturday that concentrating on California's 54 electoral votes made sense.

"The map that was presented to him was a California victory strategy. There seemed to be pretty much unanimity that California was the way to go. The pot of money is not unlimited and it has to come from somewhere," said an aide who spoke on the condition of anonymity.
Aides said resources may be pulled from Ohio and New Jersey to help fund the estimated $4 million California push.

The Times said its research found that 26 states and the District of Columbia were now leaning toward Clinton, for a total of 325 electoral votes; 13 states favoured Dole for about 101 electoral votes; and the remaining 11 states appeared too close to call. To win the presidency, 270 electoral votes are needed.
